title: Tack on Avatar
content: **List of Contents** Tack on Avatar Creating Tack on Avatar **Tack on Avatar** \- Use tack to affix a part of the 3D Garment to Avatar. \- Select the **Tack on Avatar** tool from the 3D Toolbar. **Creating Tack on Avatar** \- Select the **Tack on Avatar** tool from the 3D Toolbar. \- Navigate to the 3D Window and hover over the 3D Garment as a black guide point appears. \- Click on the desired part of the 3D garment. \- The 3D Garment will turn translucent and the Avatar becomes visible. \- A dashed black line connected to the first point on the garment will follow along the mouse cursor. \- Click on the desired part of the Avatar where the 3D Garment should be affixed to. \- The Tack is created and highlighted in yellow. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to use the "Tack on Avatar" tool to attach 3D garments to avatars in a virtual environment.

title: Tack
content: **List of Contents** Tack Creating Tack **Tack** \- Use tack to affix parts of the 3D Garment together. \- Select the **Tack** tool from the 3D Toolbar. **Creating Tack** \- Select the **Tack** tool from the 3D Toolbar. \- Navigate to the 3D Window and hover over the 3D Garment as a purple guide point appears. \- Click on the desired part of the 3D Garment. \- A dashed purple line connected to the first point on the garment will follow along the mouse cursor. \- Click on the desired part of the 3D garment to designate the attaching point. \- The Tack is created and highlighted in yellow. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to use the Tack tool to affix parts of a 3D garment in design software.

title: Edit Tack
content: **List of Contents** Edit Tack Moving Tack Adjusting Tack Property Deleting Tack **Edit Tack** \- Adjust or delete previously created Tack. \- Select the **Edit Tack** tool from the 3D toolbar. **Moving Tack** \- Tack Can be moved both in the 2D Window and the 3D Window. \- The 3D Garment will turn translucent when the **Edit Tack** tool is selected. \- To move the Tack, click and drag the point to be moved. \- Release the mouse to complete the adjustment. \- In the 2D Window, only the Tack on the 2D Pattern can be moved if were to edit an Avatar Tack. **Adjusting Tack Property** \- Select the **Edit Tack** tool from the 3D toolbar and select the tack to be edited in either the 2D or the 3D Window. \- The selected tack’s property will appear in the Property Editor. \- Enter the desired value for **THREAD LENGTH** to adjust the thread length joining the tack. **Deleting Tack** \- Select the Edit Tack tool from the 3D Toolbar and hover over the tack to be deleted. \- Right click to access the pop-up menu. \- Click DELETE. \- Or, select the tack to be deleted and hit Delete key on the keyboard. \- The selected tack will be deleted. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on editing, moving, adjusting properties, and deleting tacks in both 2D and 3D environments.

title: Emulator
content: How to use CLO Fabric Kit 2.0
content_description: Discover step-by-step instructions and tips for effectively utilizing the CLO Fabric Kit 2.0 to enhance your design projects.

title: View Manual and Tutorial Links on Tooltips
content: ### **Objective** Learn how to use tools with manual and tutorial links on tooltips. ** Location ** Main Menu ▶ Hover the Mouse Over Each Tool's Icon ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Hover the Mouse Over Each Tool's Icon → Each tool's manual and tutorial links appear as a tooltip. 2. Click **Manual**. → The manual about the selected tool appears with an internet browser. 3. Click **Tutorial**. → The tutorial about the selected tool appears with an internet browser. **※ Note:** Show or hide tooltips in [Others](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002563947-%EA%B8%B0%ED%83%80-%EC%84%A4%EC%A0%95) setting.
content_description: This webpage provides a guide to accessing manuals and tutorials for various tools through interactive tooltips in the main menu.

title: Poly Pen
content: **Poly Pen** ** ** **-** Draw polygons or curves to request design modifications in the Comment Mode. \- Comment Mode ▶ Main Menu ▶ **Poly Pen.** \- Use the Poly Pen to address changes or garment information. * Create Segment To create a segment, click and drag from a start point. Double click to complete the segment. * Create Polygon To create a polygon, click on a start point and click to shape a polygon. Double click the start point to complete the polygon. * Create Curve After starting a segment, hold down the Ctrl key and click the next point. A curve point is added. Double click to complete the curves.
content_description: The Poly Pen web page allows users to easily draw polygons or curves for requesting design modifications in Comment Mode.

title: Freeform Pen
content: **Freeform Pen** **-** Freehand lines in the Comment mode to request design modification. \- Comment Mode ▶ Main Menu ▶ **Freeform Pen.** \- Use the**Freeform Pen** in the Comment Mode to mark changes or add design detail. \- Click and drag on the 3D window while the **Freeform Pen** is selected to draw lines. \- Lines resemble pencil marks are created on the 3D Garment.
content_description: The Freeform Pen feature allows users to easily mark design modifications and add details directly on the 3D garment using freehand lines in Comment Mode.

title: Tile
content: **Tile** **** **-** Repeat recording. \- Animation Mode ▶ Animation Editor Toolbar ▶ **Repeat.** \- Select the **Repeat** tool to play the recording repeatedly. \- The animation plays repeatedly.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide users with instructions on how to utilize the Repeat tool in the Animation Editor for continuous playback of their recordings.

title: Play
content: **Play** ** ** **-** Play recorded animation. \- Animation Mode ▶ Animation Editor Toolbar ▶ **Play.** \- Click the **Play** button to play the animation. \- It stops the animation at the end of the frames.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide users with a simple interface to play recorded animations and control playback using the Animation Editor Toolbar.

title: Go to start
content: **Go to start** **-** Rewind to the start of the recording. \- Animation Mode ▶ Animation Editor Toolbar ▶ **Go to Start.** \- Select the **Go to Start** button from the toolbar to rewind to the start of the recording. \- The frame bar shifts to the beginning of the playtime.
content_description: This web page provides instructions on using the "Go to Start" feature in the Animation Editor Toolbar to quickly rewind recordings to their beginning.

title: Record
content: **Record** ** ** **-** Record a 3D Garment animation. \- Animation Mode ▶ Animation Editor Toolbar ▶ **Record** \- Click the **Record** button to start recording by frames. \- When a motion file is added, recording automatically stops when the motion finishes. \- To end the recording in the middle of the process, click the Record button again.
content_description: This web page provides a user-friendly interface for recording 3D garment animations, allowing users to easily capture and manage their animations frame by frame.

title: Edit
content: **List of Contents** Edit Edit Comment Delete Comment Edit Line **Edit** **** \- Edit and delete comments or select and move created lines. \- Comment Mode ▶ Main Menu ▶ **Edit.** **Edit Comment ** \- Hover the mouse over the comment to be edited. \- Click the comment to active the edit mode. \- Click OK to complete comment. **Delete Comment ** \- Hover the mouse over the comment to be deleted. \- The **x** button appears on the right top corner of the comment. \- The comment is deleted once the **x** button is deleted. **Edit Line ** \- Click and drag to edit lines created in the Comment mode. content: **Go to End** **-** Fast forward to the end of the recording. \- Animation Mode ▶ Animation Editor Toolbar ▶ **Go to End.** \- Click the **Go to End** button to fast forward to the end of the recording. \- The frame bar shifts to the end of the playtime.
content_description: The "Go to End" feature allows users to quickly fast forward to the conclusion of a recording with a single click, seamlessly shifting the frame bar to the end of the playtime.

title: Custom View
content: **List of Contents** Custom View Adding and Applying Custom View Saving and Opening Custom View Deleting Custom View Renaming Custom View Managing Custom View Overwrite Custom View (ver4.1.0) Delete All Custom View (ver4.1.0) **Custom View** \- Add frequently used view and easily apply to the 3D Window. \- Right click on the 3D Window to access a pop-up menu. Select **CUSTOM VIEW**. \- Or, navigate to Main Menu – Display – View Point – **CUSTOM VIEW**. ** Adding and Applying Custom View** \- Navigate to Main Menu – Display – View Point – **CUSTOM VIEW**. The Custom View Window will appear. \- Rotate the 3D Window as desired and click on the Camera icon at the top of the Custom View Window. \- Newly created custom view will be added to the list. \- Double click on the desired custom view. The 3D Window will change to the selected custom view. **Saving and Opening Custom View** \- Click on the **Save** icon at the top of the Custom View Window to save the selected custom view. \- Click on the **Open** icon at the top of the Custom View Window to open a custom view. **Deleting Custom View** \- Right click on the custom view to be deleted to access a pop-up menu. \- Select **Delete** from the pop-up menu. **Renaming Custom View** \- Right click on the custom view to be renamed to access a pop-up menu. \- Select **Rename** from the pop-up menu. \- The name field will be activated. Enter a name and hit Enter key on the keyboard. \- Or, click on the custom view to be renamed. Then, click again. \- The name field will be activated. Enter a name and hit Enter key on the keyboard. **Managing Custom View** \- Click on the Arrow icon to hide or expand the Custom View Window. \- To move, click and drag the Custom View Window. **Overwrite Custom View (ver4.1.0)** \- Overwrite Custom Views. \- Set the 3D view as needed and right click on the custom view to be overwritten. \- The, Selected **Overwrite**. **Delete All Custom View (ver4.1.0)** \- Delete all views in the Custom View window at once. \- Right click on the Custom View window and select **Delete All Custom View**. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for managing custom views in the 3D Window, detailing how to add, apply, save, open, delete, rename, and organize custom views effectively.

title: Open/Save Trim
content: **List of Contents** Save Trim Open Trim **Save Trim** \- Save OBJ files as Trims. \- Trim files can be previewed in CLO Library and glue to 3D Garments once they are imported to the 3D window. \- Navigate to Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ **OBJ** When loading an OBJ file, opt Load as Trim. \- Select the desired OBJ file when saving if there are multiple OBJs loaded to the file you are working on. \- Navigate to Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ **Trim** The OBJ file is saved as a Trim file. ** Open Trim** * **Open with File Open Window ** \- Navigate to Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶**Trim** When the Open Trim window appears, designate where the Trim will be placed in the 3D window with the Position option. \- When you select Original, the Trim will be placed where it was when the file was saved. \- When you select **Reset (0,0),** the Trim will be placed at the center of the 3D grid. * **Open with the Livrary Window ** \- When the Trim file is hovered over in the Library window, its preview appears. \- Double click or click and drag the Trim file to the 3D window in order to open the file. \- When the Open Trim window appears, designate where the Trim will be placed in the 3D window with the Position option. \- When you select Original, the Trim will be placed where it was when the file was saved. \- When you select **Reset (0,0),** the Trim will be placed at the center of the 3D grid. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for saving and opening Trim files in a 3D garment design software, detailing the steps for importing OBJ files as Trims and positioning them within the 3D workspace.

title: Change Focus for Camera
content: **Change Focus for Camera** \- Automatically change camera’s focus based on the selected object. \- The view is rotated based on the selected object. \- Select the object and right click on the mouse while controlling the view. \- The view rotates fiducial to the selected object.

title: ISO Topstitch Preset
content: **ISO Topstitch Preset** \- Download ISO Topstitch from the Library window. \- Library ▶ Download ▶ Hardware and Trims ▶ Topstitch ▶ **ISO_Standard**. \- Click the desired Topstitch and drag and drop to the Object Browser. \- Selected ISO Topstitch is added to the Object Browser.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for downloading and adding the ISO Topstitch preset to your Object Browser from the Library window.

title: Pleats Sewing
content: **List of Contents** Pleats Sewing Using Pleats Sewing **Pleats Sewing ** \- Easily sew pleats pattern to another pattern. \- Select the **Pleats Sewing** tool from the 2D toolbar. **Using Pleats Sewing ** \- In order to use the **Pleats Sewing** tool to sew pleats pattern to its paired pattern, both patterns should have Internal Lines with the same offset. Also, the ratio between the pleats pattern’s number of lines, including both Pattern outlines and Internal Lines, and the paired pattern’s number of lines should be 3:1. \- Additionally, segment points should be added to the intersection of Pattern outlines and Internal Lines. \- After achieving above conditions, select the Pleats Sewing tool from the 2D toolbar and navigate to the 2D Window. \- Be careful and always establish the sewing line on the paired pattern first. The **Pleats Sewing** tool would not work properly when such caution is not taken. \- Click on the either end of the Pattern outline where the first half of the pleats sewing line will be established on. The sewing direction should be equal to the pleats direction. \- Drag the mouse cursor towards the sewing direction and click again to complete the first half of the sewing line. \- Then, hover the mouse over the pleats pattern’s Pattern Outline. click on the either end of the pattern to designate the start point of the second half of the pleats sewing line. \- Drag the mouse towards the sewing direction and click again to complete. \- The second half of the sewing line’s direction must be the same as the first half of the sewing line’s direction. \- Now the pleats sewing lines are completed. \- Please use the **Free Sewing** tool when sewing accordion pleats. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on using the Pleats Sewing tool to effectively sew pleats patterns to their paired patterns in a 2D design environment.

title: Automated Arrangement Point Creation
content: **Automated Arrangement Point Creation** \- Load an Avatar by navigating to Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ. \- **Automatically Add Arrangement Points** option under Load OBJ window ▶ Load as Avatar is selected by default. \- Arrangement Points and Bounding Volumes are automatically created sized to the loaded OBJ. **※Note****: ** This option works properly only when imported OBJ is either in T or A pose and below error message appears when this function cannot be applied properly. ‘Arrangement Points were not fitted to the avatar. The avatar must be in a T-pose of A-pose’
content_description: This web page provides guidance on how to automatically create arrangement points for avatars by importing OBJ files, with specific instructions for ensuring the avatar is in the correct pose for optimal functionality.

title: 3D Garment Surface Textures - Save
content: **Objective** Save all texture images used on Garments and subsidiary Materials to a designated folder. Surface textures can also be cropped to a desired size before they are saved (ver2.5.0). ** Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ **Surface Textures** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ **Surface Textures** → The Save File window appears. 2. Select a Folder location to save the Surface Textures, then press **Save**. → The Save Surface Textures window appears. 3. Select from the available settings. **Original Size** | Saves the surface textures in its original size. ---|--- **Crop Fabric Textures** | Crops the image file based on the value entered. 4. Click **OK**. → The selected image size setting is applied and the files are saved to the Folder location assigned. **※ Note:** Surface textures refers to the surface texture of a Garment.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for saving and cropping garment surface texture images to a designated folder.

title: [Print Layout Mode] Roll Width
content: **List of Contents** Roll Width Roll Width Properties **Roll Width** \- Adjust the width of the fabric roll in the Print Layout Mode. \- Main Menu ▶ Simulation Mode Button ▶ **PRINT LAYOUT**. **Roll Width Properties** \- Select the **Edit Texture** tool from the 3D toolbar. Then, select the Pattern with a texture to be edited. → The selected texture's properties appear in the Property Editor. \- Adjust **Width** and **Position** under the **Roll** option (ver5.0.0.) \- For **Width** , select a preset from the drop-down menu on the right, or insert specific values to either the **in** or **mm** option. \- Change the fabric placement with the **Position** option (ver5.0.0.) → The fabric placement changes based on the inserted values. Go back to the List of Contents

title: Convert to Avatar
content: **List of Contents** Convert to Avatar Load 3D Body File Align 3D Body and CLO Avatar Save Converted Avatar **Convert to Avatar ** \- Convert 3D dummies or body scans to CLO avatars maintaining their body shapes. \- Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ **Convert to Avatar ** **Load 3D Body file ** \- Navigate to Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ **Convert to Avatar** \- Load a 3D body file, preferably in attention pose, as a reference for the conversion. \- Select the CLO Avatar to be converted with the 3D body file. \- Click **Next**. **Align 3D Body and CLO Avatar ** * **Change Avatar Pose ** \- Select the Pose folder corresponding to the loaded Avatar. \- Load attention pose. \- Check **Joint Rotation Only** and select **OK**. * **Align Height and Inseam with Avatar Size Editor ** \- Select **Open Avatar Size Editor**. \- Adjust **Height** to align the shoulder height between the CLO Avatar and the 3D body. \- Adjust **Inseam** to align the crotch height between the CLO Avatar and the 3D body. \- Once the adjustment is completed, close the Avatar Size Editor. * **Align Avatar Joints** \- Align all joints: total body, ankle, arm, and neck. \- Make sure to align above four locations as closely as possible for more accurate conversion. \- Select **Convert** once all adjustments are completed. **Save Converted Avatar ** \- Rotate to check the quality of the converted avatar. \- Click **Save as Avatar** to save the converted avatar when it's satisfactory. \- When additional modification is needed, click **Back** to repeat previous steps. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for converting 3D body files into CLO avatars while ensuring accurate alignment and customization.

title: Show Style Line
content: ### **Objective ** Express and emphasize style lines, silhouette, internal/external lines, fold lines of 3D Garments. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Show Style Lines (Alt+0)** 3D Window ▶ 3D Garment Display Icon ▶ **Show Style Lines** (ver5.0 or later) **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below:** **Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ 3D Garment ▶**Show Style Lines (Alt+0)** 3D Window ▶ 3D Garment Display Icon ▶ **Show Style Lines** (ver5.0 or later)** **→ The Style Line window and Style Lines are now being displayed on the 3D Garment. 2. title: Change Pose by OBJ Morphing
content: **Objective** Vertex Morphing has a merit of maintaining avatar's final form without any distortion. However on the other hand, garments may fall off during the morphing process, especially when there is a large difference between the first and the last pose as the pose changes by the minimum distances between points in the avatar rather than the units of avatar joints. Therefore if a big difference between the poses, it is recommended to create an OBJ file for interim pose and morph stage-by-stage. If it is inconvenience, change pose by another method, [Change Pose by Using Collada](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002633147). **Operation** 1. After dressing an avatar in CLO, at least two files are required to change poses such as T-pose avatar and another avatar in desired pose. Export both of the files in OBJ format. To find export method in details, check [3D File (OBJ) Import/Export ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000494107) for the reference. 2. Click File ▶ Import ▶ **OBJ** and select the T-pose OBJ file of the previously exported avatar. Click **OK** on the option dialogue to load the avatar. 3. Put the garments on top of the loaded avatar. 4. Click File ▶ Import ▶ **Morph Target** and load the previously saved avatar with another pose. Set the 'Morphing Frame Count' in the option dialogue, then click **OK**. 5. The **Simulation** button automatically activates and the avatar pose slowly changes according to the set frame count. The garment also starts simulating in accordance with the change. Adjust garments if necessary, after the final pose simulation.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for effectively using Vertex Morphing in CLO to maintain garment integrity during avatar pose transitions.
